checks.command: .venv/bin/python -I scratchpad/audit090/probe_ship.py (ship progression bypass probes, temp projects only)
.venv/bin/python -I scratchpad/audit090/probe_goal.py (goal render encoding probes, temp projects only)
evidence_class_errors over all 94 plan*.md files of the repo (no false positive)

findings.rule: fail-safe: a malformed plan must not let ship pass (FR-002 / AC-002 '/spec-ship requires it')
findings.evidence: _require_release_evidence only calls pending_release_evidence, which keeps steps whose classes == ('release',) and ignores orphans. Probe (temp project, spec+plan reviewed): '**Evidence class:** release (signing)', a step with the release line twice, or the release line under '## Steps' (not matched by _PLAN_SECTION) all give `livespec validate plan.md` errors but `require_progression(..., 'ship')` returns READY (release_evidence() == []). /spec-ship only runs `--progression ship`, so an invalid or unparsable release declaration silently ships without its proof.
findings.correction: In _require_release_evidence (or release_evidence), read plan.md and raise ProgressionBlocked('release_evidence_invalid:' + ';'.join(evidence_class_errors(text))) when evidence_class_errors is non-empty, before computing pending items; add a ship test for an unknown class, a duplicated class and an orphan release line.

findings.rule: robustness: placeholder detection of release proofs
findings.evidence: A proof cell is accepted unless it equals exactly one of '', '-', '—', 'pending', 'tbd', 'todo', 'n/a'. Probe: '| 2 | pending notarization |' and '| 2 | not yet produced |' mark the step satisfied and ship returns READY.
findings.correction: Reject cells whose first word is a placeholder (pending, tbd, todo, n/a, none, not, waiting, '?', en dash) or require the proof to name a receipt path/identifier; add tests.

findings.rule: robustness: fenced code is not skipped in implementation.md
findings.evidence:
recorded_release_proofs scans every line, unlike plan_steps which skips fences. Probe: an example block ```markdown
## Release Evidence
| 2 | example |
``` inside implementation.md satisfies step 2 and ship returns READY.
findings.correction: Reuse the _FENCE tracking of plan_steps in recorded_release_proofs so fenced examples (and the rows they contain) are ignored.

findings.evidence: release_evidence reads implementation.md whenever plan.md exists, even when no step is release-class, and lets UnicodeDecodeError/OSError escape. Probe: a single invalid UTF-8 byte in implementation.md makes `livespec goal render spec-implement --feature <f>` exit 1 with an uncaught UnicodeDecodeError traceback from plan_evidence.py, for features that declare no release step (new failure surface for every implement goal).
findings.correction: Return early when no step is release-class before reading implementation.md, and convert decode/OS errors into a domain error (ProgressionBlocked in the gate; an explicit pending_release_evidence error or controlled CLI message in goal render).

findings.rule: robustness: silent fail-open on unrecognised declarations
findings.evidence: _CLASS_LINE only matches lines starting with optional spaces/bullet then '**Evidence class:**'. A declaration in a blockquote ('> **Evidence class:** release'), in a table cell, with '__Evidence class:__', or after text on the same line is neither a class nor an orphan: validate reports nothing and the step is local (probe: blockquote -> validate [] and ship READY).
findings.correction: Detect any line containing 'Evidence class' (case-insensitive, outside fences) that the strict pattern does not parse and report it as a malformed declaration in evidence_class_errors.

findings.rule: robustness: step identity is the ordinal, not the declared step number or title
findings.evidence: PlanStep.number = len(steps)+1 and proofs are keyed only by that integer. A plan whose heading says 'Step 5' but is the 2nd step is reported as 'step 2: Step 5 — ...' and a proof row '| 5 | ... |' is ignored (probe). After a plan edit renumbers steps (and a re-review), an older proof row keyed by number can satisfy a different release step; the proof is never bound to the step title.
findings.correction: Use the number written in a 'Step N' heading when present, and bind the proof row to the step (e.g. require the title or a stable step id in the row, or store the plan step title next to the proof and compare).

findings.evidence: _CLASS_LINE ends with lazy '(.*?)\s*$': a class line followed by many spaces is O(n^2). Measured: 16,000 trailing spaces then a character -> 0.9 s for one line (4x input ~ 16x time), so a crafted plan line can stall validate and goal render.
findings.correction: Capture '(.*)' and strip in Python, or use '(\S(?:.*\S)?)?\s*$'.

findings.rule: robustness: a later placeholder row does not revoke an earlier proof
findings.evidence: Rows '| 2 | signed |' then '| 2 | pending |' keep step 2 satisfied (placeholders are skipped, last non-placeholder wins).
findings.correction: Let the last row for a step win, including placeholders, or report duplicate step rows.

findings.evidence: _plain strips '_' so 'tests/test_plan_evidence_class.py' becomes 'tests/testplanevidenceclass.py' in step titles exposed in pending_release_evidence and release_evidence_pending messages (observed on the 090 plan).
findings.correction: Strip only emphasis markers that wrap words, or keep the raw title for display.

findings.evidence: Prompts are excluded from the stable identity (review_stability.reviewed_snapshot), so keeping PROMPT_VERSION='2' keeps current plan reviews valid, as decided. Side effects: reviews prepared before 090 count as current although the reviewer never received the minimal-scope rule; and the plan prompt is ~430 chars longer, which feeds the 'fits' budget check, so a plan near --review-max-chars can now split into a different batch partition (identity change) or an indivisible section can become over budget.
findings.correction: Document both effects in the changelog/decision; optionally exclude the constant rule text from the budget computation or reserve it in the budget.

findings.rule: compatibility: goal hash now depends on implementation.md
findings.evidence: runtime_context is part of the hashed canonical payload; recording a release proof in implementation.md during /spec-implement (as the skill instructs) removes the pending item, changes goal_hash and triggers goal recompilation, which resets the outcome task and re-validates carried evidence. Contracts without release steps keep their bytes (key omitted), as intended.
findings.correction: Accept and document, or keep satisfied items in the list with their status so the hash changes only when the plan changes.

findings.evidence: goal_payload.py grows from 294 to 313 lines (above the 300-line target given for this review; the project gate target is 400/limit 500, so the conventions gate passes). _release_context returns dict[str, Any] and release_evidence returns list[dict[str, object]] without a TypedDict, while python.md asks for justified Any and explicit domain types.
findings.correction: Move _release_context next to goal_delivery_lane (validator/delivery/goal.py) or into plan_evidence, and type the pending item as a TypedDict (feature, step, evidence, status, proof).

findings.evidence: The rules package uses relative imports; the new import is absolute ('from validator.plan_evidence import ...').

'Out of scope: changing what /spec-ship requires' contradicts AC-002 ('/spec-ship requires it') and the in-scope ship progression added to spec-ship. The plan summary still names validator/goal_tasks.py and 'the conventions pack' while the code changes goal_payload.py and system/minimal-spec-scope.md.
findings.correction: Reword the out-of-scope line (e.g. 'other /spec-ship requirements') and align the plan summary with D-01/D-03.

findings.evidence: The progression destination list is duplicated here instead of reusing progression_gate.PROGRESSION_DESTINATIONS added by this diff.
findings.correction: Import PROGRESSION_DESTINATIONS (lazily if import cost matters) and check membership against it.
